group_results.reason: The changed unpack signature carries a key context. The target reaches unpack through its existing calls, with a null context at the root.
A keyed nested object type error can receive a key-specific diagnostic, but none of the target's formats requests a nested object.
Object member keys are forwarded to nested unpacking, but the target's only object member format uses the type-agnostic `o` token.
The keyed array type diagnostic requires an array token nested under an object key; the target supplies no such format.
For a nonempty parsed array, the existing `[o!]` call reaches the changed array-element call that passes a null key context.
The string wrong-type diagnostic can include an object key, but the target has no keyed string format.
The target has no keyed `i` format to reach the changed integer type diagnostic.
The target has no keyed `I` format to reach the changed integer type diagnostic.
The target has no keyed boolean format to reach the changed boolean type diagnostic.
The target has no keyed real format to reach the changed real type diagnostic.
The target has no keyed number format to reach the changed number type diagnostic.
The target has no keyed null-validation format to reach the changed null type diagnostic.
Every existing json_unpack call enters json_vunpack_ex and reaches the changed root call with a null key.
This change adds API-suite assertions for error text. The fuzz target neither runs that suite nor contains those assertions.

build.reason: The supplied build recipe delegates to test/ossfuzz/ossfuzz.sh, whose contents are absent. The Makefile names this target but does not resolve the delegated build path.

input.reason: The entry consumes finite fuzzer bytes as a selector followed by a length-delimited JSON buffer; accepted object and array values can reach the unpack calls.

lifecycle.reason: The target checks the parsed root, releases a successful deep copy, frees dumped text and its reparsed value, and decrements the root after unpacking. The `o` unpack token returns a borrowed value without incrementing its reference count.

control_flow.reason: The entry reaches unpack, but all three formats are fixed. The object-member format uses `o`, which accepts any nonnull JSON type, so fuzzer bytes cannot select the changed keyed wrong-type diagnostic branches.

accepted.requirement: The unpack operation must be able to validate a typed value under an object key and expose the supported wrong-type diagnostic containing that key.
accepted.target_route: LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput parses a JSON object, then invokes json_unpack through json_vunpack_ex, unpack_object, and nested unpack.
accepted.failure_condition: A valid JSON object with a wrong-typed member, such as an integer `data` member for a keyed string format, cannot trigger the diagnostic: the target fixes its member format to `{s?o}` and passes no error object through json_unpack.
accepted.alternative_paths: Changing JSON bytes cannot change the fixed format. The root `o` and array `[o!]` calls also use the type-agnostic `o` token; the target has no error-capable unpack call that exposes the new text.
